jane_s: Hey team — customer CI started failing after we bumped redwood-python from 1.2.7 -> 1.3.0. macOS arm64 runners. ImportError: cannot import name 'Mapping' from 'typing_extensions'. Repro in poetry v1.6.0. pyproject has extras "httpx,aio". stack below. anyone seen this?

jane_s: ```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/bin/pytest", line 8, in <module>
    from redwood.client import RedwoodClient
ImportError: cannot import name 'Mapping' from 'typing_extensions' (/opt/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.10.9/x64/lib/python3.10/site-packages/typing_extensions/__init__.py)
```

emily_support: thanks for the report — can you paste your pyproject.toml and `poetry lock` sha? also which python runtime exactly (3.10.x?) and are you using the lockfile pinned to poetry? :mag:

jane_s: python 3.10.9 (GH actions macos-latest). pyproject has `redwood-sdk = {version = "^1.3.0", extras = ["httpx"]}`. lockfile attached in ticket.

raj_engineering: quick suspicion: this looks like typing_extensions api moved between versions and one of the extras pulls a newer typing_extensions requiring a different import path. which httpx/aiohttp versions are resolving in the lock? can you run `pip list | grep typing-extensions` in the failing env?

jane_s: `pip list` from job: `typing-extensions 4.6.0`

tasha_sdk: that version *should* still expose Mapping but there are known macOS arm wheels some deps ship that trigger import resolution surprises. two quick reproduction attempts: (1) try a clean venv `python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install poetry && poetry install --no-dev --no-root` (2) try forcing typing-extensions==4.5.0 as a test. also can you paste the resolved extras from the lock (the package versions)?

jane_s: tried clean venv, same failure. forcing typing-extensions==4.5.0 makes the import move forward but then httpx resolves to some httpcore 0.17 wheel that fails due to c-extensions missing on arm64. so easing typing-extensions breaks binary deps.

raj_engineering: OK that's useful — two conflicting constraints: typing-extensions API surface vs httpcore binary wheel ABI on mac arm64. we should avoid forcing typing-extensions for customers. patch idea: release a small SDK patch that removes direct imports relying on legacy typing_extensions symbols and use typing import fallback: `from typing import Mapping` when available, fallback to typing_extensions otherwise. can you open a minimal repro (Docker or GH action) for us?

jane_s: I'll try to create a minimal GH action repro. quick question: is there a supported matrix for macos arm64 in 1.3.0? not sure if we changed any transitive deps.

emily_support: not that I'm aware of; we support macos in CI but we don't test every combination of extras. please cc me when you open the repro so I can escalate. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: reproduced on macos-latest (python 3.10.9) — same ImportError. job log: https://ci.example/12345

tasha_sdk: thanks, opened internal tracking: SDK-issue-#834. short-term workaround for customers: avoid installing `redwood-sdk[httpx]` on macos arm64 runners — instead install minimal deps and use our hosted API or run on linux runners. or pin a compatible httpcore that has arm64 wheels, e.g. `httpcore==0.16.3` (if that builds), but caveat: building c-extensions in CI may be slow.

raj_engineering: long-term we'll release a 1.3.1 that removes the problematic typing_extensions import and updates extras metadata to steer users to compatible httpcore/httpx combos. ETA: 48-72h after a short PR and test.

jane_s: thanks folks — I'll add repro and link SDK-issue-#834. will try linux runner as temporary mitigation and notify the customer.

emily_support: perfect — ping when you have the GH action. I'll prepare a templated reply for the customer explaining the root cause (typing_extensions api change + arm64 wheels) and the workaround + expected SDK patch window.

tasha_sdk: internal note: also consider adding an extras marker for macos/arm64 in pyproject so `redwood-sdk[httpx]` doesn't auto-resolve to incompatible transitive wheels on that platform.

jane_s: filed repro GH action: https://github.com/simplecorp/repro/actions/runs/98765 — reproduces in 2 steps. thanks everyone.
